meta.notes: RS = Rüstungsschutz (Armor Rating). BE = Behinderung (Encumbrance). Weights in Stein (1 Stein = 1 kg). Prices in Silbertaler. Armor supplements (helms, limb armor) marked with +RS indicating additive bonus. Metal armor interferes with magic (see magic_restriction field).

armor.name: Thick Clothing
armor.special: RS does not add to any armor worn over it. Includes winter/fur clothing, all-leather wilderness clothing, heavy leather jackets over street clothing, certain brocade and velvet festival garments.

armor.name: Quilted Underclothing
armor.special: Required under all metal armor (chain, plate) to prevent abrasions and pressure sores. RS and BE do not add to the value of armor worn over it; listed values apply only when worn alone.

armor.name: Quilted Surcoat (Gambeson)
armor.special: Two layers of coarse linen or padding, stitched to form tubes and pockets stuffed with horsehair or seagrass. Ideal under a cuirass or light plate (RS and BE then add). Can also be worn alone as it absorbs blunt force.

armor.name: Toadskin
armor.special: Vest of thick leather with heavy rivets. Popular with Thorwalers. Encumbrance not added to Swimming or Body Control (Balance) checks. Only PRO 2 vs ranged attacks. Metal BE counts as 1 for magic purposes.

armor.name: Leather Harness
armor.special: Hard leather armor produced by cooking multi-layer leather in hot wax. Usually in form of human torso with additional shoulder reinforcement. Provides one level of protection against Cold (AA variant). At Heat level II+: +1 Heat level to maximum 4.

armor.name: Cuirass
armor.special: Roughly anatomically shaped breastplate of solid steel, held by two leather straps crossing at the back. Popular with light cavalry and foot soldiers.

armor.name: Chainmail (Half-sleeve)
armor.special: Closely interwoven mesh of wire rings. Fluid fall for the protection offered, but quite heavy. Half-sleeved. PRO 5 vs Bows, Crossbows, Daggers, and Swords combat techniques.

armor.name: Iryan Armor
armor.special: Variant of leather armor. Fireproof: wearer immune to DP from fire and fire-based attacks. Without 8+ hours maintenance per week: penalties increase to -2 MOV, -2 INI.

armor.name: Linothorax Armor
armor.special: Variant of cloth armor. PRO 3 vs Blunt Weapons and Two-Handed Blunt Weapons. When catches fire: -2 penalty to Body Control checks to extinguish.

armor.name: Scale Mail
armor.special: Leather with sewn-on (often riveted) bronze scales, lined with felt inside. Increasingly expensive traditional armor of the Aventurian Northwest. PRO 6 vs Blunt Weapons and Two-Handed Blunt Weapons. Only PRO 2 vs Daggers.

armor.name: Mirror Armor
armor.special: Typical armor of Tulamydian potentates: finest chain mesh with inset or mounted plate sections. Usually richly decorated. PRO 5 vs Swords and Two-Handed Swords. Only PRO 2 vs Blunt Weapons and Two-Handed Blunt Weapons.

armor.name: Light Plate
armor.special: Steel chest and back armor (breast and back each in two overlapping pieces for mobility) with lamellar skirts for thighs. Popular with cavalry and pikemen.

armor.name: Long Chainmail
armor.special: Full-sleeved, approximately thigh-length chainmail.

armor.name: Half Plate
armor.special: Variant of plate armor. PRO 7 vs Daggers and Fencing Weapons. Only PRO 1 vs attacks from the rear.

armor.name: Gareth Plate
armor.special: Heavy but mobile infantry armor protecting from collar bones to knees and fingertips. Entirely of sliding plate sections. Usually combined with a sallet.

armor.name: Horasian Cavalry Armor
armor.special: Complete set: sliding chest and back armor with long leg protection, neck/shoulder/arm armor, armored gauntlets, and visorless helmet. Cannot be meaningfully combined with other armor pieces.

armor.name: Full Tournament Armor
armor.special: Designed for cavalry tournament riders. Made-to-measure and decorated with engravings, punching, etc. A 'sporting equipment' and status piece for those who can afford it.

armor.name: Leather Helm
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+1 RS, +1 BE). Usually just a skull cap of hardened boiled leather with a layer of felt padding. Sometimes additional edge and seam reinforcements.

armor.name: Morion
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+2 RS, +1 BE). Helmet type widespread in Horasian Empire with front and rear upturned brim.

armor.name: Sallet (with Bevor)
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+2 RS, +1 BE). Garetian helmet type with usually wide neck protection and often a flip visor. Worn with steel 'bevor' (neck and chin protection).

armor.name: Storm Cap (Sallet)
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+2 RS, +1 BE). Close-fitting, deep-pulled helmet without brim or visor.

armor.name: Pot Helm
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+2 RS, +2 BE). Massive, visorless iron helmet of roughly cylindrical form, often with flat helmet top. Now obsolete cavalry helmet type.

armor.name: Plate Helm (Tellerhelm)
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+1 RS, +1 BE). Metal skull cap with wide brim. Popular with sappers.

armor.name: Baburiner Hat
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+2 RS, +1 BE). Leather helm reinforced with metal pieces, long neck protection of chain strips. Widespread throughout Tulamydian cultural sphere.

armor.name: Chain Coif
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+1 RS, +1 BE). Close-fitting coif with shoulder protection. Requires quilted underclothing.

armor.name: Chain Limb Armor
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+1 RS, +1 BE). Forearm, lower leg, and sometimes shoulder protection in chainmail, plus gauntlets and greaves.

armor.name: Leather Limb Armor
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+1 RS, +1 BE). Forearm, lower leg, and sometimes shoulder protection in leather.

armor.name: Plate Limb Armor
armor.special: Additive armor piece (+2 RS, +2 BE). Full plate protection for limbs.

armor.name: Chainmail Vest
armor.special: Short chain vest without sleeves.

armor.name: Buckler
armor.special: Small fist shield. Worn on the forearm or held in the fist. Counts as improvised parry weapon. Can be used with most one-handed weapons.

armor.name: Small Shield
armor.special: Standard small round or oval shield. Grants PA bonus. Does not count as encumbrance if used with a one-handed weapon.

armor.name: Medium Shield
armor.special: Standard kite or heater shield. Provides cover to part of torso (AR 1 against ranged attacks if held raised). Reduces INI by 1.

armor.name: Large Shield
armor.special: Tower or wall shield. Provides substantial cover (AR 1 against ranged attacks to front). Reduces INI by 2 and movement. Requires STR 14+ to use effectively.

armor.name: War Shield
armor.special: Reinforced combat shield with metal boss and rim. Can be used offensively (shield bash: 1d6 DP). Requires STR 15+ to use effectively.

armor.name: Spiked Shield
armor.special: Medium shield with metal spikes. Can make offensive spike attacks: 1d6+1 DP. Spikes can catch weapons on critical hit, disarming opponent on failed STR check.
